It brings together daily health signals (resting heart rate, sleep, fatigue, exercise, mood, radiation dose and cabin conditions) and checks them against transparent, explainable rules based on NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight. OrbitCare is decision support, not diagnosis: it supports the mission medical team, and every value is labelled as simulated or real, current or stale. Role-based access keeps health records private. details:
What it does
OrbitCare is a web-based health monitoring and self-care support system for astronauts on long-duration missions, where contact with Earth can be delayed or lost. A crew member records daily signals: resting heart rate, sleep, fatigue, exercise, mood and stress, radiation dose and cabin conditions such as CO2. A rules engine checks them against explainable rules built around NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight and returns one of four results: no flag, review, priority review, or insufficient data.

How it works

  • A personal dashboard compares each vital with the person’s own baseline.
  • Five Hazards pages monitor radiation, isolation and wellbeing, distance and autonomy, gravity and physical condition, and the environment.
  • An interactive Body Map shows 11 clickable regions. Each one shows its status, vitals and trends, the hazards affecting it, what the crew member can do now, and when to escalate.
  • ORBIT, a rule-based assistant, answers health questions offline. Chats stay on the device and sync when the link returns.
  • Reports, CSV export and role-based access (astronaut, medical officer, administrator) keep health records private.

Benefits and intended impact
Crews can spot slow health trends earlier, understand what their signals mean, and act confidently during communication blackouts. Ground teams get a structured history when contact resumes. The same approach could support remote clinics, polar stations and other isolated communities on Earth.

Tools and technologies
Laravel 12 (PHP), MySQL, Blade, Bootstrap 5, vanilla JavaScript, Chart.js, inline SVG with CSS animation, and 56 automated tests (229 assertions). Developed with XAMPP and VS Code, with AI-assisted coding that our team reviewed and tested.

Creativity
The Body Map turns many numbers into one visual picture a crew member can read in seconds. Its heartbeat follows the real resting heart rate, and every status uses an icon and text, not colour alone. Every screen shares one rules engine as its single source of truth, so no two screens can disagree.

Factors we considered
OrbitCare is decision support, not diagnosis, and it supports the mission medical team. All data is simulated because no raw astronaut datasets were available, and every value is labelled simulation or real, current or stale. Alert thresholds are team assumptions that would need clinical review. We also designed for offline use, privacy by role, keyboard access and reduced-motion preferences.
